props.note: Described as a kind; no composition, test conditions or data are given.

props.name: zinc oxide catalyst with potassium hydroxide (alkali)
ammonium precipitation for best results
props.statement: Because alkali metals modify its catalytic properties, the (non-fusible) zinc-chromium catalyst must be precipitated with ammonium compounds for best results; precipitating zinc sulfate as a chromate with ammonium chromate or bichromate, then drying and igniting, gives a very satisfactory methanol catalyst.

props.name: co attacks steels
props.statement: Carbon monoxide attacks the steels usually employed in the ammonia synthesis, so corrosion is more serious in the methanol process; the ammonia catalyst cannot be employed in the methanol synthesis.

props.name: copper zinc oxide methane runaway
props.statement: Adding copper to zinc oxide definitely improves its methanol-forming properties, but as the temperature is raised the combination begins to form methane, and in large synthesis units a run-away temperature is the almost inevitable result.

props.name: dehydration terms environment dependent
props.note: Larson states he relied on Sabatier's published results for chromium oxide as a dehydrating agent (cited)
props.statement: Whether chromium oxide or aluminum oxide is the better dehydrating catalyst may depend on experimental conditions; characterizing a material as dehydrating or dehydrogenating requires defining the reaction environment carefully.

props.name: difficultly reducible oxides
props.statement: Several difficultly reducible oxides promote the methanol-forming properties of zinc oxide, but most also encourage secondary reactions that make them valueless when methanol is the sole objective; aluminum oxide gives largely dimethyl ether.

props.name: koh retards methanol
props.statement: Potassium hydroxide retards the methanol reaction on zinc oxide catalysts and favors the formation of a large number of primary and secondary alcohols.

props.name: manufacture exclude poisons
props.statement: Because small quantities of certain substances adversely affect a catalyst, large-scale catalyst manufacture must rigidly exclude all poisonous materials while permitting effective inclusion of the desired promoters.

props.name: many products from co h2
props.statement: The products of the interaction of carbon monoxide and hydrogen are numerous and often depend on the catalyst; theoretically their equilibria are so favorable that synthesizing methanol to the exclusion of other organic compounds might seem hopeless.

props.name: methanol catalysts lower temperature
props.statement: Methanol catalysts are reactive at appreciably lower temperatures than ammonia catalysts; most methanol catalysts operate between 350 and 400 °C (the abstract prints 354 °).

props.name: no methanol at 1 atm
props.statement: Equilibrium calculations show that practically no methanol can be formed at atmospheric pressure, and higher pressures are required at the operating temperatures of practical catalysts.

props.name: no synthesis decomposition correlation
props.note: the decomposition rates are Sabatier's results, cited from his work
props.statement: There is very little correlation between the rates of methanol synthesis and the rates of methanol decomposition produced by metal oxides.

props.name: partially reduced cuo deactivates
props.statement: Partially reduced copper oxide catalyzes the methanol synthesis but soon becomes inactive, the loss increasing rapidly with temperature.

props.name: pressure at least 200 atm
props.statement: Because it takes about 10 times as long to produce the second half of the equilibrium as the first half, practical operating pressures are at least 200 atm; the DuPont plant at Belle, West Virginia, uses 700 atm.

props.name: reproducibility details
props.statement: Irreproducibility of catalyst results is mostly due to failure to recognize and record even the minutest experimental details, not to faulty measurement.

props.name: sulfur no effect zno cr2o3
props.statement: Sulfur (sulfur compounds) has no poisoning effect on the zinc oxide-chromic oxide methanol catalyst, so low-cost sulfates can be used as starting materials.

props.name: zno cr2o3 confines to methanol
props.statement: Chromic oxide is one of the most effective means of improving the methanol-forming properties of zinc oxide, and zinc oxide-chromic oxide is one of the few combinations that confine the reaction to methanol over a wide range of temperature.

props.name: alumina dehydration dme
props.statement: The dimethyl ether produced with aluminum oxide is explained by aluminum oxide being an excellent dehydrating agent.

props.name: unreduced oxide promoter copper
props.statement: Copper catalysts slowly reduced at low temperature contained some unreduced oxide, which might have exercised a promoter action on the reduced metal.

props.name: zno partial reduction
props.statement: Zinc oxide may be at least partially reduced to the metal by carbon monoxide and hydrogen, which would explain why it catalyzes methanol formation though it hardly decomposes methanol; substances that accelerate its reduction might improve zinc oxide.
